name: FluxNative – AI Chatbot, Product Writer & Mobile App for WooCommerce
author: fluxnative

sections.description:
FluxNative adds an AI chat to your WooCommerce store. It answers shoppers from your own products, policies and orders, in their language, and shows prices and stock as cards from your data, with Add to cart. The same plugin writes your product descriptions and connects your store to native iOS and Android apps.

Every feature works for free with your own AI key. You don’t need a FluxNative account, and nothing is locked.

AI chat that answers from your store

  • Finds products by need: “something light for a beach wedding”, “a thermos” or a search in another language finds the right products, not only those with the same words. Shoppers can also send a photo of an item to find similar products (10 photos a visitor a day; photos of people or documents are refused).
  • Helps shoppers buy. It offers Add to cart for any product, sizes and colours too, prices the cart with their coupons and shipping, and after an add can show up to three products that go with it: your cross-sells first, then what other orders on your site bought together.
  • Answers after the sale: where an order is, with tracking links from Shipment Tracking or Advanced Shipment Tracking (guests by order number and billing e-mail), and shipping and return questions from the policy pages you pick, with a link to the page. Signed-in shoppers can cancel an order or ask for a refund from its card, after a confirm; the AI never does it.
  • Prices, stock, links and addresses appear only as cards from your data. Every reply is checked so it never states a figure or a link your data does not hold.
  • It always says it is an AI assistant and never books, orders or pays. “Talk to a person” is always there, with your ways in your order: WhatsApp, Zalo, Messenger, Telegram, LINE, Instagram, Viber, a call, a text, e-mail, a link, or a message left by e-mail.
  • Signed-in shoppers can turn on Memory, so the chat keeps their sizes, budget and style across chats. They see, change and delete it.

Stores, marketplaces, directories and blogs

  • WooCommerce stores: products with their variations and stock, the cart, shipping, returns and orders.
  • Marketplaces (Dokan, WCFM): who sells each product, a seller’s rating and own policies, seller comparisons, and “ask this seller” questions sent to the seller.
  • Directories (Listeo, MyListing): places by need, “open now” and distance, answers from the listing’s own fields, and real availability with a Book button.
  • News and blogs: answers from your articles with links to them, a summary of the article being read, and what to read next.

See what shoppers ask

Insights, on the AI chat tab, shows questions a day, answered and not, hand-offs, thumbs, add to cart from the chat and the orders that followed, credits, and the questions it could not answer and the searches that found nothing. It does not say who asked, and exports to CSV. Turn on Keep chats to read whole chats (off by default, kept 30 days unless you change it).

Product and listing writer

Write a product description from a few keywords in one click on the product screen, in your shoppers’ languages and your tone, then review it before you save. Translate descriptions, and show shoppers what reviews say about a product in a few lines, refreshed when a review is added. For Listeo and MyListing it writes listing descriptions and replies to reviews.

Your key, your limits

  • Use OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, OpenRouter or any OpenAI-compatible service with your own key (stored encrypted), or link your FluxNative account and spend its credits.
  • You set the models, which features are on, a limit per person, per visitor and per minute, and a monthly spend cap. Repeated questions are answered from a cache.
  • Search by intent keeps your catalogue’s embeddings in your own database, up to 25,000 products. With FluxNative credits it costs a credit per 25 products indexed, once (searches are free), and your plan sets how many products are indexed. With your own key it needs an embedding model: OpenAI, Google Gemini and OpenRouter have one, and an OpenAI-compatible service when you name one. Anthropic has none, so with Anthropic the chat uses your store’s keyword search.
  • Installing the plugin sends nothing anywhere: no usage tracking, no statistics, no calls home. Each service under External services is contacted only after you set it up.

Light on your site

The chat is one small script without jQuery, loaded only on the pages you choose. Nothing loads in WP admin outside the plugin’s own pages and the product screen’s writer box.

Your store as a mobile app

When you want iOS and Android apps, this plugin is already their connection to your store. It reads the data WooCommerce, Dokan, WCFM, Listeo, MyListing and the delivery plugins keep, and checks every request so each person sees only their own orders, products and bookings.

Site health checks what usually breaks a store’s app: a firewall or security plugin blocking the REST API, plain permalinks, a cache serving old answers, PHP warnings in answers. Each problem comes with the one setting to change.

One step on FluxNative turns your store into a native app, an optional service with its own plans: https://fluxnative.app/wordpress

Works with the plugins your store runs

WPML, Polylang, TranslatePress, currency switchers, Subscriptions, Bookings, Appointments, Product Bundles, product add-ons, gift cards, points, wallet, delivery dates, rentals, auctions and composite products.

External services

The plugin connects to outside services only for the features you turn on, and only from your server (except Cloudflare Turnstile, which runs in the visitor’s browser when you set it up).

The AI provider you choose receives, for each AI call: the visitor’s question and the last messages of the conversation, your site’s name, and what the chat’s tools found for it: product, category, variation and review texts, the visitor’s cart lines and totals, your policy pages’ passages and shipping zones, sellers’ public profiles and policies, listings’ public fields and reviews, articles’ passages, and for an order question the order’s number, status, date, total, item names and tracking (never an address, a phone or an e-mail). For a signed-in shopper who turned on the assistant’s memory, the preferences it keeps for them (sizes, budget, style, what they like or avoid, in their words). A seller in the app asking about their store sends their own sales figures and waiting orders. The writer sends the product’s or listing’s facts and your keywords. Search by intent sends product texts when they are indexed and the shopper’s search. With Photo search on, a photo a visitor sends with a message is sent once to the provider, shrunk to at most 512 pixels (384 for Gemini, 768 for FluxNative and other OpenAI-compatible services) and re-encoded without its EXIF data, to say what it shows; a photo of a person or a document is not used for search. Your site keeps no copy, and later messages send only the provider’s short description of the item. Your key is sent only to that provider.

  • OpenAI (https://openai.com, calls go to api.openai.com), when you pick OpenAI: Terms https://openai.com/policies/terms-of-use, Privacy https://openai.com/policies/privacy-policy.
  • Anthropic (https://www.anthropic.com, calls go to api.anthropic.com), when you pick Anthropic: Terms https://www.anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms, Privacy https://www.anthropic.com/legal/privacy.
  • Google Gemini API (https://ai.google.dev, calls go to generativelanguage.googleapis.com), when you pick Google Gemini: Terms https://aistudio.google.com/docs/terms, Privacy https://policies.google.com/privacy.
  • OpenRouter (https://openrouter.ai), when you pick OpenRouter, which passes the call to the model you name: Terms https://openrouter.ai/terms, Privacy https://openrouter.ai/privacy.
  • An OpenAI-compatible service at the address you enter: that service’s own terms and privacy policy apply.

FluxNative (https://fluxnative.app), only when you choose “Use FluxNative credits” on the AI chat tab. Linking sends your site’s address, its name and a random install id to https://api.fluxnative.app and shows a code you approve on fluxnative.app in your browser (no password is typed in WordPress). After that, each AI call sends the same AI call data as above, with the site’s address and install id, to FluxNative’s AI service, which passes it to its model provider and counts the call’s credits on your account; the AI chat tab also reads your credit balance from it. With search by intent on credits, once you click Index products on the AI chat tab, your published products’ texts (name, categories, tags, options, descriptions; never prices of a cart, orders or people) are sent in batches to FluxNative’s own embedding model, and later a shopper’s search words; FluxNative keeps neither, and the resulting vectors are stored only in your site’s database. While linked, the plugin also asks FluxNative once a day (and on Check FluxNative) for the public ids of your FluxNative apps that run on this site and shows them on Mobile app › Sign-in and App links as a suggestion; nothing is saved until you review them and click Apply. It sends only the site’s address and install id, and receives only public ids (no key). FluxNative cannot change your site’s settings, users or content. Unlink on the AI chat tab to stop. The “See your store as an app” button (Overview and the Mobile app tab) only opens https://fluxnative.app/wordpress in your browser with your store’s address filled in; the plugin itself sends nothing then. Terms: https://fluxnative.app/terms. Privacy: https://fluxnative.app/privacy#wordpress.

Cloudflare Turnstile (https://www.cloudflare.com/products/turnstile/), only when you enter Turnstile keys for the site chat: after the number of messages you set, the visitor’s browser loads Turnstile’s script from https://challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/api.js (Cloudflare serves it only from there), and your server sends its answer and the visitor’s address to https://challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/siteverify to check it. Terms: https://www.cloudflare.com/website-terms/. Privacy: https://www.cloudflare.com/turnstile-privacy-policy/.

Cloudflare’s address list (https://www.cloudflare.com/ips/), only when you turn on Behind Cloudflare on the Advanced tab: when you turn it on and once a day after, your server downloads https://www.cloudflare.com/ips-v4 and https://www.cloudflare.com/ips-v6, the address ranges Cloudflare publishes, so the plugin believes the visitor address Cloudflare names only on Cloudflare’s own requests. Nothing about your site or its visitors is sent. Terms: https://www.cloudflare.com/website-terms/. Privacy: https://www.cloudflare.com/privacypolicy/.

The “Talk to a person” buttons are the links you set: WhatsApp (wa.me), Zalo (zalo.me), Messenger (m.me), Telegram (t.me), LINE (line.me), Instagram (ig.me), Viber, a call (tel:), a text (sms:), e-mail (mailto:) or a page of your own. The visitor’s device opens them; the plugin sends nothing to those services. A message left in the chat goes from your site by e-mail (wp_mail) to you, or to the seller or listing owner it was for.

The site health check, “Check files” under App links on the Mobile app tab and “Check again” under Talk to a person on the AI chat tab (which reads your home page as visitors get it, to suggest contact buttons) call your own site’s address; nothing leaves your server.

The plugin sends nothing anywhere when it is installed and activated: no usage tracking, no statistics, no calls home. Each service above is contacted only after you set it up.

Firebase Cloud Messaging (Google): only when push notifications have a Firebase service account. Each push to an Android phone (its title, text, the screen it opens and the phone’s push token) goes to fcm.googleapis.com, and the plugin gets its access at oauth2.googleapis.com with a token signed by that account. Terms: https://firebase.google.com/terms. Privacy: https://policies.google.com/privacy.

Apple Push Notification service: only when push notifications have an APNs key. Each push to an iPhone (its title, text, the screen it opens and the phone’s push token) goes to api.push.apple.com (api.sandbox.push.apple.com for a development build of your app). Terms: https://developer.apple.com/support/terms/. Privacy: https://www.apple.com/legal/privacy/.

Payment gateways, for payments in the app: only for a gateway whose WooCommerce plugin you already set up, and only when a shopper pays an order in the app. The plugin uses the keys that gateway’s plugin keeps, and sends the gateway what a checkout on your website would: the order’s number, total and currency, and the shopper’s name, e-mail and phone where the gateway’s page needs them. A gateway in test mode uses its own test host (for example api-m.sandbox.paypal.com or apitest.myfatoorah.com). Each gateway’s own terms apply:

  • Stripe (api.stripe.com): Terms https://stripe.com/legal/ssa, Privacy https://stripe.com/privacy.
  • Razorpay (api.razorpay.com): Terms https://razorpay.com/terms/, Privacy https://razorpay.com/privacy-policy/.
  • PayPal (api-m.paypal.com): Terms https://www.paypal.com/legalhub/home, Privacy https://www.paypal.com/us/privacy-center/home.
  • Paystack (api.paystack.co): Terms https://paystack.com/terms, Privacy https://paystack.com/privacy/merchant.
  • Flutterwave (api.flutterwave.com): Terms https://flutterwave.com/us/terms, Privacy https://flutterwave.com/us/privacy-notice.
  • Mercado Pago (api.mercadopago.com): Terms and privacy https://www.mercadopago.com.ar/ayuda/terminos-y-politicas_194.
  • MyFatoorah (api.myfatoorah.com, or api-sa.myfatoorah.com, api-ae.myfatoorah.com, api-qa.myfatoorah.com or api-eg.myfatoorah.com for an account in Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Qatar or Egypt): Terms https://www.myfatoorah.com/en/terms-and-conditions/, Privacy https://www.myfatoorah.com/en/privacy-policy/.

Sign in for your app (only the methods you set up under Mobile app › Sign-in):

  • Google sign-in: the plugin downloads Google’s public keys from https://www.googleapis.com/oauth2/v3/certs to check the sign-in tokens your app sends. Nothing about the shopper is sent to Google. Terms: https://policies.google.com/terms. Privacy: https://policies.google.com/privacy.
  • Sign in with Apple: the plugin downloads Apple’s public keys from https://appleid.apple.com/auth/keys to check the identity tokens your app sends. Nothing about the shopper is sent to Apple. Terms: https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/. Privacy: https://www.apple.com/legal/privacy/.
  • Facebook Login (Meta): only when you enter your Facebook app’s ID and secret. When a shopper signs in with Facebook, your server sends the access token the app got, with your app’s ID and secret, to https://graph.facebook.com (debug_token) to check the token was issued for your app, then reads that person’s Facebook id, name and e-mail (me). Terms: https://developers.facebook.com/terms/. Privacy: https://www.facebook.com/privacy/policy/.
  • Firebase (Google): for phone sign-in the plugin downloads Firebase’s public keys from https://www.googleapis.com/robot/v1/metadata/x509/securetoken@system.gserviceaccount.com. When you upload a Firebase service account, the plugin gets an access token from https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token and, when an account is deleted on your site, deletes that person’s Firebase user (its id, wp: and the WordPress user id) at https://identitytoolkit.googleapis.com. Terms: https://firebase.google.com/terms. Privacy: https://firebase.google.com/support/privacy.
sections.installation:
1. In WP admin, go to Plugins › Add New, search for FluxNative, then Install and Activate.
  2. Open FluxNative in the admin menu. Overview shows what is set up, your site’s health and the next step.
  3. On the AI chat tab, under Setup, paste your AI provider’s key (or choose FluxNative credits) and tick Site chat bubble; pick a look under Chat look and save.
  4. Open a product in WP admin to use the AI description box.
sections.faq:
Do I need a FluxNative account?

No. The AI features work with your own AI key. A FluxNative account is only needed to spend FluxNative credits or to build a mobile app.

Where is my AI key kept?

In your WordPress database, encrypted with your site’s salts. It is never shown again, sent to shoppers or written to a log. Changing your site’s salts means pasting the key again.

How do I keep AI costs down?

Pick a small model (the defaults are), keep the monthly spend cap, set limits per person and per visitor, and turn on the chat only on the pages that need it. Repeated first questions and review summaries are answered from a cache.

Is anything locked or paid?

No. Every feature in the plugin works for free with your own AI key. FluxNative credits are an optional way to pay for AI calls without a key, and building a mobile app on FluxNative is an optional service with its own plans.

Does the plugin send data anywhere when I install it?

No. Nothing leaves your site until you set up an AI provider, link FluxNative, or turn on push notifications or payments in the app. Each service and what it receives is listed under External services. Chats are not kept unless you turn on Keep chats.

Where is the source of the chat’s scripts?

assets/site-chat.js, site-chat-panel.js and site-chat-demo.js are bundled with esbuild (spaces removed, names kept) from the readable files in assets/source/site-chat/src/. To build them again: npm install esbuild@0.28 in that folder, then node build.mjs --out ../.. there. Every other script and all PHP files ship as written.

Where are proof-of-delivery pictures kept?

In the uploads folder’s fluxnative-private/proof/, outside the media library, with random names and files that refuse web requests on Apache and IIS. On nginx add location ^~ /wp-content/uploads/fluxnative-private/ { deny all; } to the site’s server block, or move the folder outside the web root with the fluxnative_proof_dir filter: add_filter( 'fluxnative_proof_dir', fn () => dirname( ABSPATH ) . '/fluxnative-proof' );. Only the order’s driver, its seller and shop managers open them. They are deleted with the order, by WordPress’ personal-data eraser, and when the plugin is uninstalled.

Where are pictures sent in app messages kept?

In the uploads folder’s fluxnative-private/messages/, with random names and the same files that refuse web requests (the nginx rule above covers it too). The app never gets their file address: each person of the conversation gets a signed link that opens the picture for a day.

How do store administrators and staff sign in to the seller app?

On the website. A seller or store manager app made with FluxNative opens your site’s own login page, so two-factor and your other login protections apply, then asks the administrator to allow the app. The app gets a session for the seller area only, never a password or a WordPress credential. It works only for the return address your app has in Mobile app › App links › Seller app sign-in, which you add or apply from FluxNative there. Shop managers and other store staff can also sign in with their password, Google or Apple in the app, unless two-factor is on for their account (Two Factor, Wordfence Login Security or WP 2FA, or another plugin through the fluxnative_user_requires_browser_sign_in filter): then they sign in on the website too, and app sessions they made before turning it on stop, so the two-factor step is never skipped.

Does it work with the MStore API plugin?

Yes. Both can run on one site; each answers its own apps.
sections.changelog:
0.2.1

  • Photo search with Anthropic: Claude Haiku 5.5 (the default model) and other Claude models that think before they answer no longer reply “The assistant could not answer”. The plugin turns thinking off where the model allows it and gives more room where it does not.
  • AI chat with Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Fable models no longer fails on its tool rounds.

0.2.0

  • Listeo directories in the app work as on your website: the booking calendar with day prices, Listeo’s itemised price, coupons, booking details, tickets for Listeo’s Ticket Check, and Delete as Listeo hides a booking.
  • Listing owners in the app: Listeo’s submit form and packages, hide, renew and delete, their bookings with Approve, Reject, Cancel, Confirm payment and Renew, manual bookings, the calendar and iCal, ticket checks and replies to reviews.
  • Explore: Listeo’s place search, listing types and their categories, price, rating, guests, dates, open now, your search fields and sort menu, and map pins.
  • Listing pages: related and nearby listings, the owner’s profile, claims with Listeo’s paid plans, reports, bookmarks and views on the account, and contact details as Listeo’s visibility setting shows them (in the AI chat too).
  • Messages in the app are Listeo’s own conversations, shared with your website’s Messages page.
  • Dokan stores: opening hours, the map, sorting, the contact form and each seller’s sub-order; product reviews and downloads on every store.
  • Your website’s pages open signed in from the app (a one-time link), Listeo’s guest and owner switch, and owner sign up where Listeo offers it.
  • Faster listing search and map pins with price and rating filters.
  • The store manager app on a plain WooCommerce store: orders, products, coupons and sales for shop managers and administrators, by WooCommerce’s own capabilities and its Analytics settings. Administrators, and store staff with two-factor on (Two Factor, Wordfence Login Security, WP 2FA), sign in on the website (two-factor included) to the app’s registered return address only; app sessions reach only their own app’s routes.

0.1.0

  • First version.
  • AI chat for stores, marketplaces (Dokan, WCFM), directories (Listeo, MyListing) and blogs: search by intent and by photo, cards from your own data, “Talk to a person”, memory for signed-in shoppers, and Insights. Your own AI key (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, OpenRouter, OpenAI-compatible) or FluxNative credits, with limits and a monthly spend cap.
  • Product and listing writer, translations and review summaries.
  • The connection for your FluxNative mobile apps: sign-in (password, Google, Apple, phone), cart and checkout with your WooCommerce gateways, messages, push notifications and app links; the seller app for Dokan and WCFM and the driver app with proof of delivery.
  • Works with the plugins your store already runs: WPML, Polylang, TranslatePress, currency switchers, Subscriptions, Bookings, Appointments, Product Bundles, product add-ons, gift cards, points, wallet, delivery dates, rentals, auctions and composite products.
  • One admin page with Overview, AI chat, Mobile app, Payments and Advanced tabs, site health checks for apps, and Behind Cloudflare for correct visitor limits.

After that, each AI call sends the same AI call data as above, with the site’s address and install id, to FluxNative’s AI service, which passes it to its model provider and counts the call’s credits on your account; the AI chat tab also reads your credit balance from it. With search by intent on credits, once you click Index products on the AI chat tab, your published products’ texts (name, categories, tags, options, descriptions; never prices of a cart, orders or people) are sent in batches to FluxNative’s own embedding model, and later a shopper’s search words; FluxNative keeps neither, and the resulting vectors are stored only in your site’s database. While linked, the plugin also asks FluxNative once a day (and on Check FluxNative) for the public ids of your FluxNative apps that run on this site and shows them on Mobile app › Sign-in and App links as a suggestion; nothing is saved until you review them and click Apply. It sends only the site’s address and install id, and receives only public ids (no key). FluxNative cannot change your site’s settings, users or content. Unlink on the AI chat tab to stop. The “See your store as an app” button (Overview and the Mobile app tab) only opens https://fluxnative.app/wordpress in your browser with your store’s address filled in; the plugin itself sends nothing then. Terms: https://fluxnative.app/terms. Privacy: https://fluxnative.app/privacy#wordpress.

Cloudflare Turnstile (https://www.cloudflare.com/products/turnstile/), only when you enter Turnstile keys for the site chat: after the number of messages you set, the visitor’s browser loads Turnstile’s script from https://challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/api.js (Cloudflare serves it only from there), and your server sends its answer and the visitor’s address to https://challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/siteverify to check it. Terms: https://www.cloudflare.com/website-terms/. Privacy: https://www.cloudflare.com/turnstile-privacy-policy/.

Cloudflare’s address list (https://www.cloudflare.com/ips/), only when you turn on Behind Cloudflare on the Advanced tab: when you turn it on and once a day after, your server downloads https://www.cloudflare.com/ips-v4 and https://www.cloudflare.com/ips-v6, the address ranges Cloudflare publishes, so the plugin believes the visitor address Cloudflare names only on Cloudflare’s own requests. Nothing about your site or its visitors is sent. Terms: https://www.cloudflare.com/website-terms/. Privacy: https://www.cloudflare.com/privacypolicy/.

The “Talk to a person” buttons are the links you set: WhatsApp (wa.me), Zalo (zalo.me), Messenger (m.me), Telegram (t.me), LINE (line.me), Instagram (ig.me), Viber, a call (tel:), a text (sms:), e-mail (mailto:) or a page of your own. The visitor’s device opens them; the plugin sends nothing to those services. A message left in the chat goes from your site by e-mail (wp_mail) to you, or to the seller or listing owner it was for.

The site health check, “Check files” under App links on the Mobile app tab and “Check again” under Talk to a person on the AI chat tab (which reads your home page as visitors get it, to suggest contact buttons) call your own site’s address; nothing leaves your server.

The plugin sends nothing anywhere when it is installed and activated: no usage tracking, no statistics, no calls home. Each service above is contacted only after you set it up.

Firebase Cloud Messaging (Google): only when push notifications have a Firebase service account. Each push to an Android phone (its title, text, the screen it opens and the phone’s push token) goes to fcm.googleapis.com, and the plugin gets its access at oauth2.googleapis.com with a token signed by that account. Terms: https://firebase.google.com/terms. Privacy: https://policies.google.com/privacy.

Apple Push Notification service: only when push notifications have an APNs key. Each push to an iPhone (its title, text, the screen it opens and the phone’s push token) goes to api.push.apple.com (api.sandbox.push.apple.com for a development build of your app). Terms: https://developer.apple.com/support/terms/. Privacy: https://www.apple.com/legal/privacy/.

Payment gateways, for payments in the app: only for a gateway whose WooCommerce plugin you already set up, and only when a shopper pays an order in the app. The plugin uses the keys that gateway’s plugin keeps, and sends the gateway what a checkout on your website would: the order’s number, total and currency, and the shopper’s name, e-mail and phone where the gateway’s page needs them. A gateway in test mode uses its own test host (for example api-m.sandbox.paypal.com or apitest.myfatoorah.com). Each gateway’s own terms apply:

  • Stripe (api.stripe.com): Terms https://stripe.com/legal/ssa, Privacy https://stripe.com/privacy.
  • Razorpay (api.razorpay.com): Terms https://razorpay.com/terms/, Privacy https://razorpay.com/privacy-policy/.
  • PayPal (api-m.paypal.com): Terms https://www.paypal.com/legalhub/home, Privacy https://www.paypal.com/us/privacy-center/home.
  • Paystack (api.paystack.co): Terms https://paystack.com/terms, Privacy https://paystack.com/privacy/merchant.
  • Flutterwave (api.flutterwave.com): Terms https://flutterwave.com/us/terms, Privacy https://flutterwave.com/us/privacy-notice.
  • Mercado Pago (api.mercadopago.com): Terms and privacy https://www.mercadopago.com.ar/ayuda/terminos-y-politicas_194.
  • MyFatoorah (api.myfatoorah.com, or api-sa.myfatoorah.com, api-ae.myfatoorah.com, api-qa.myfatoorah.com or api-eg.myfatoorah.com for an account in Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Qatar or Egypt): Terms https://www.myfatoorah.com/en/terms-and-conditions/, Privacy https://www.myfatoorah.com/en/privacy-policy/.

Sign in for your app (only the methods you set up under Mobile app › Sign-in):

  • Google sign-in: the plugin downloads Google’s public keys from https://www.googleapis.com/oauth2/v3/certs to check the sign-in tokens your app sends. Nothing about the shopper is sent to Google. Terms: https://policies.google.com/terms. Privacy: https://policies.google.com/privacy.
  • Sign in with Apple: the plugin downloads Apple’s public keys from https://appleid.apple.com/auth/keys to check the identity tokens your app sends. Nothing about the shopper is sent to Apple. Terms: https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/. Privacy: https://www.apple.com/legal/privacy/.
  • Facebook Login (Meta): only when you enter your Facebook app’s ID and secret. When a shopper signs in with Facebook, your server sends the access token the app got, with your app’s ID and secret, to https://graph.facebook.com (debug_token) to check the token was issued for your app, then reads that person’s Facebook id, name and e-mail (me). Terms: https://developers.facebook.com/terms/. Privacy: https://www.facebook.com/privacy/policy/.
  • Firebase (Google): for phone sign-in the plugin downloads Firebase’s public keys from https://www.googleapis.com/robot/v1/metadata/x509/securetoken@system.gserviceaccount.com. When you upload a Firebase service account, the plugin gets an access token from https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token and, when an account is deleted on your site, deletes that person’s Firebase user (its id, wp: and the WordPress user id) at https://identitytoolkit.googleapis.com. Terms: https://firebase.google.com/terms. Privacy: https://firebase.google.com/support/privacy.
